$comment: Brave browser extensions — DECLARATIVE source of truth.
Each entry is force-installed via Chromium's External Extensions
mechanism: brave.nix writes
~/.config/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/External Extensions/<id>.json
with `external_update_url` pointing at the Chrome Web Store. Brave
auto-fetches + auto-updates the extension on next launch and CANNOT
be uninstalled via the UI (force-installed extensions show a 'managed
by your organization' badge).
Why this mechanism:
programs.chromium.extensions = [...] from home-manager only works
for the chromium-proper package, NOT for Brave. Brave silently
ignores it. The External Extensions/<id>.json route is what KDE
Plasma Integration, Brave's own internal extensions, and any
enterprise policy uses — supported across all Chromium-derivatives.
Adding a new extension:
1. Find the extension on https://chromewebstore.google.com
2. The 32-char ID is the last segment of the URL
3. Add the entry below + run build.sh switch + relaunch Brave
Removing one: delete entry, switch, relaunch — Brave drops it on next start.
Schema: extensions.<id>.{name, rationale}
